newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: SOCCER-GUATEMALA STADIUM NEEDS BIG CHANGES POST-TRAGEDY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GUATEMALA STADIUM NEEDS BIG CHANGES POST-TRAGEDY.

text.p: Guatemala's Mateo Flores stadium, closed since October when 78 soccer fans died in a tragic crush in the stands, needs major changes before it can reopen, a world soccer official said Friday.
Hugo Salcedo, a representative of FIFA, World Cup soccer's governing body, inspected the stadium Friday and met with sports directors to review their plans for improvements.
To reopen the stadium, authorities must install seats, devices to prevent bottlenecks at entrances, screening for false tickets, and improved exits in case of panic, Salcedo told Reuters.
"We also need to know more specifically what is the stadium's total capacity because there are three different numbers now and we don't know exactly what it is," Salcedo said.

Separate investigations by a Guatemalan presidential commission, the state prosecutor's office and independent experts all concluded that extreme overcrowding led to a human avalanche in the cement terraces at one end of the stadium.
As many as 60,000 people may have been in the stadium for the October 16, World Cup qualifying match between Guatemala and Costa Rica, according to state prosecutor Selvin Galindo.
In a study after the disaster, which took place about half an hour before the game was to begin, a group of Guatemalan engineers determined the stadium's capacity was between 32,000 and 35,000.

Galindo has brought criminal charges against 18 stadium workers and sports events promoters, accused of responsibility for the overcrowding. The judge assigned to the cases has not yet decided whether they will go to trial.
Salcedo said he was reviewing plans by the Guatemalan National Soccer Federation and the Guatemalan Automonous Sports Confederation to make the improvements to the stadium.
Salcedo said he couldn't speculate when the stadium could receive FIFA permission to reopen.
"It will depend on what the sports directors themselves have planned and when they will finish their work," he said.
Salcedo said a publicity campaign about changes in the stadium was important.

He said Guatemalan soccer fans would have to get used to the idea maintaining clear aisles between groups of individual seats instead of the traditional, general admission cement terraces which had no aisles.
